_about: Factory settings: the one place for their values (core/settings.js reads them). This file holds the shared defaults and is tracked by Git. Personal changes go to settings/local.json next to it (ignored by Git; the editor's settings write it): the same structure, only the keys that change; objects merge key by key, other values replace. An empty object here is an open map, and so is an object marked "_open": true: any keys may be added under it. The API key is never here. provider.use: who draws the cards, "api" (the image model of the preset) or "codex-cli". provider.preset (core/providers/preset.js): the service every keyed call goes to — images when use is "api", the vision model (hero, look) and the text model (set plans, text help) — "openrouter" or "google" (Google AI Studio, the Gemini API: core/providers/gemini.js); each preset has its block below with the same keys. provider.openrouter (core/providers/openrouter.js) and provider.google: endpoint, model = the image model id, visionModel = the vision model that looks at finished cards, textModel = the text model that writes set plans and text help, fallbackModel = the model tried in the same attempt when the main one fails (an error, a refusal, an answer without an image; null = none), aspectRatio = the ratio wanted for a card, never taller than the card (the author's decision, clarified 2026-10-31, Scapes BASE_RULES.md «Формат карточки»: the model image is scaled down to the card and only its sides are cut, equally — nothing from the top or the bottom; a model is asked for this ratio when its profile takes it, else for the closest ratio of its profile that is not taller than the card: core/providers/models.js, core/image/prepare.js), keyEnvVar = the environment variable (or the line of .env in the project root) that holds the key, params = any other request fields passed as is to every model (a model's own profile params are added over them; for google they are generationConfig fields), timeout per call in ms, retries on HTTP 429/5xx and the backoff before the first retry in ms. provider.google.prices: the Gemini API's answers carry no cost, so it is computed from their token counts: per model id (an open map) a list of price periods in USD per 1M tokens — input, output (text and thinking), imageOutput (image tokens of the answer) — each held through its `until` day (UTC), the last without one. provider.models (core/providers/models.js): the profile of each image model, keyed by its id ("codex-cli" for Codex), an open map ("_open": a profile for any model may be added): aspectRatios = the ratios it accepts (null = any, said in words), maxReferences = input images one request may carry (more is refused before anything is sent), params = request fields this model needs, prompt = how its provider advises writing prompts, source = where these facts come from and when they were checked, framing = a sentence added at the end of this model's image prompt, its own correction of the hero's size and margins where it draws them off the style's (none set: on 2026-10-30 a «draw it larger» sentence for Nano Banana, whose hero box is about 0.45 of the card against 0.55–0.58 on the references, made one hero larger and one smaller, and Codex did not follow a «less, with sky above the heads» sentence at all; Codex's top margin is helped by its ratio instead, provider.codexCli), sameAs = the id of the same model at another service (its profile fills the fields this one lacks, and the style's starting post-processing of that id applies); a model without a profile is asked for 1:1 with no extra fields. provider.codexCli (core/providers/codex-cli.js; Codex's own login, no per-image payment): the command, the orchestrating model (null = the user's Codex config), the aspect ratio said in the brief (1:1, by the rule of provider.<preset>.aspectRatio; measured 2026-10-30 before that rule: the space above the hero on the same orders, median of 5, was about 18 px at 4:5 and 36 px at 1:1; the reference cards: 58–75 px), timeout in ms, reasoning effort, sandbox, and the prompt template ({refs} = legend of attached images, {brief} = the card prompt). card: attempts = how many generations of one card one `card make` run may spend at most; maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one run in USD, checked before every paid call. editPrompt = the whole prompt of `card edit` ({wish}), sent with the card's model image as the input image; editLegend = how Codex is told what the attached image is. card.pick (core/card/pick.js): when a run leaves a card with two versions or more (and made one of them), the vision model sees the best maxVersions of them at once (by the program's order: what the vision model saw outweighs measured FAILs) with what was found in each, and names the best with a short reason; that version becomes the card (chosenBy "look"), the pick recorded in the run's last attempt (pick.json); asked only when the run's spend cap leaves room for about one look per version shown, with the vision model's reasoning and timeout; use = on or off, maxTokens per answer, template {title} {order} {count} {versions}, version {n} {wish} {findings}, wish {wish}, clean = a version with nothing found; between versions without such problems it judges like an art director which is better as a card (reads at once, more expressive, more appealing detail, closer to the style's reference cards; small measured deviations — colour, size by the bible — do not decide), shown up to `references` of the style's reference cards the order's prompt picked (same staging, before the versions, each after refLabel; refsNote and refsLead fill {refsNote} and {refsLead} when there are any) (the author's decisions of 2026-10-31). card.fix (core/card/fix.js): learning from a failed picture — before a new attempt whose earlier attempt has findings (a FAIL of the style's checks, a problem the vision model saw), the preset's textModel (with the reasoning and timeout of set.plan) writes a correction in plain positive sentences that is added at the end of the prompt; the loop does it for its own next attempt, `card regenerate` for the attempt it starts from (a wish is then not required; the person's wish outranks the findings); use = on or off, maxTokens per answer, template ({prompt} {findings} {previous} {wish}), previous ({fix} = the correction the failed attempt already carried), wish ({wish}); propose ({language} {notes} {title} {prompt} {findings}) and proposeNotes ({notes}) = the wish the editor's text help proposes for a card (`card wish`, editor operation proposeCardWish), languages = the language codes it writes in. tuneProcessing = after each generation search the post-processing settings per card (core/card/tune.js, bounds in styles/<style>/processing.json); false = apply the starting settings as they are. processing: post-processing settings per model (core/image/adjust.js settings object; the key is the image model id, or "codex-cli"), only to override the style's own starting settings (styles/<style>/processing.json → start). vision: how the preset's visionModel is asked (through the preset's endpoint and key): format = the answer convention of its family (a key of FORMATS in core/card/hero.js), reasoning = the request's reasoning field (null = not sent; OpenRouter gets it as is, Google gets {effort} as thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel; gemini-3.8-flash refuses reasoning turned off and takes the efforts low, medium and high; the vision model is gemini-4-argon by the author's decision of 2026-10-31 (look, «drawing»: it alone found the drawing errors of the review cards, about $0.009 more per attempt than gemini-3.8-flash; at OpenRouter the same model is google/gemini-4-argon, $2 / $10 per 1M tokens, checked at openrouter.ai/api/v1/models 2026-10-31), low effort is enough), timeout per call in ms. hero (core/card/hero.js): finding the hero's outline for the checks when no agent or person gives its box — the vision model gives the box and the outline is cut inside it; mirrorCheck = ask also on the mirror image of the card and trust the outline only when the two boxes overlap at least agreeIou (intersection over union); maxTokens per answer (the model's reasoning counts in it: 400 cut the answers of gemini-3.8-flash); prompt.template with {width} {height} {hero} {answer}, and the hero's words for an object card or a scene ({what} = the order's subject, object or scene). look (core/card/look.js): the vision model looks at every attempt, when a key is there, and says whether the picture is what the order asked for and holds nothing unordered; use = on or off (an agent that looks at every card itself may turn it off), maxTokens per answer, blocking = the order questions whose "no" makes the loop regenerate (the other questions and the style's checklist for eyes go to the report; caption is not blocking: a caption that does not name the subject is usually the plan's error, which a new picture does not fix; drawing = errors of the drawing itself — anatomy, gaze, repeated parts that should match, fused objects — added 2026-10-31 after the author's review: on 14 attempts of the Mars collection only gemini-4-argon with this question found the missing arm, the gaze into nowhere, the 3×4 against 4×4 solar cells and the drops without a source, gemini-3.8-flash at low and high effort found none of them), prompt: template ({title} = the caption, {order} = the assembled prompt without its note on reference images, {questions}, {checklist} = the style's checklist for eyes of the attempt, {answer}), wish ({wish} = the person's words of the attempt), questions (the key names the kind of problem), answer ({json} = the answer's shape, built from the question keys). set (core/set): parallel = cards of one set made at the same time; maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one set's cards in USD (each card also keeps card.maxSpendUsd). set.cards.maxCount: the most loose cards one run of «Создать карточки» / `ccf.mjs cards make` asks for (the author's decision, 2026-10-30: 1 to 10 per run; loose cards are not checked against the collection's sets). set.plan: how the preset's textModel writes set plans when no agent does (the editor's path; through the preset's endpoint and key): repairs = how many times the plan's rule errors are sent back to the model for a fix (a plan that passes the program's checks is read once more by the text model against the same brief, prompt.glue.review of the style's set-rules.json: what it finds goes back as one repair while repairs are left, else to the plan's warnings), retries = how many more times the same request is sent when an answer cannot be read as JSON (empty, cut, prose), per plan and per self-check, before it counts as an error, keepVersions = how many earlier plans a set keeps in its set.json `planVersions` when its plan is replaced (set save --set),maxTokens and temperature per answer (Google: temperature is not sent, Gemini 3.6+ ignore it), reasoning = as in vision (null = not sent), timeout per call in ms, maxSpendUsd = the spend cap of one planning run (a set with its variants, or a whole collection) in USD. text.help (core/text/draft.js): the editor's text help, which turns a producer's rough notes in a free-text field into the finished text with the preset's textModel (and the reasoning and timeout of set.plan): maxTokens per answer (the bound of one call's price) and temperature; template ({what} {form} {context} {notes}); kinds = one entry per field it serves (what the text is, its form); contextLead = the line before what the text belongs to; context = how each piece of it is said ({value}); propose ({what} {form} {context} {language}) and proposeLead = an empty field: the text is proposed from what it belongs to, in the page's language (the names: card.fix.languages). editor (editor/server.mjs): port = the local port the editor listens on (when taken, a free one is used); openBrowser = open the browser when the editor starts.

google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1.prompt: Google: describe the scene as a narrative paragraph, not a keyword list (subject, action, setting, composition, style); say what is wanted, not what is not ("an empty street", not "no cars"); name placement and empty space in words; say what each attached image is for and how it relates to the new image. Framing: give the shot and the camera in words (Google's own example: "Medium-full shot, center-framed"; "low angle", "wide-angle") and anchor placement to things in the picture rather than to left and right, which the model sometimes swaps; Nano Banana 2 tends to add things nobody asked for, so name what the picture holds.
google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1.source: openrouter.ai/google/gemini-nano-banana-2.1 (aspect_ratio list, "an unlisted value is rejected"; input_references up to 14; resolution 1K | 2K | 4K; n = 1), checked 2026-10-30; prompting: cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana (2026-03-06, Nano Banana 2 and Pro) and ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation; "occasional confusion around spatial localisation (e.g. left/right)": deepmind.google/models/model-cards/nano-banana-2-1 (2026-10-06); anchoring placement to things in the scene: picsart.com/blog/nano-banana-2-1-prompts (2026-10-07, not Google); added objects: a community comparison of GPT Image 2 and Nano Banana 2 (youtube.com/watch?v=l284Xo8NOgE, 2026-05-18), checked 2026-10-31

openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare.prompt: OpenAI: a consistent order — scene, subject, key details, constraints; short labelled segments read better than one long paragraph; name materials, light, colours and the medium; give each input image a number and a role; short exclusions such as "no extra text, no watermark" are allowed at the end. Framing: describe body framing, relative scale and gaze (OpenAI's own example: "full body visible, feet included") and the placement of the subject and of empty space; favour simplicity over detail.
openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare.source: openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare (aspect_ratio list, no resolution field, quality auto | low | medium | high | xhigh | max, input_references up to 16), checked 2026-10-30; prompting: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-prompting (gpt-image-2.5-flare and -sunburst; framing quotes re-read 2026-10-31)

gemini-nano-banana-2.1.source: the same model through the Gemini API: ai.google.dev/api/generate-content (ImageConfig: the same 14 aspect ratios; imageSize 1K | 2K | 4K, uppercase K) and ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation (up to 14 reference images; Nano Banana 2.1 table: 4:5 at 1K = 928x1152, 1120 tokens), checked 2026-10-30

codex-cli.prompt: Codex draws with OpenAI's image tool: as for GPT Image; the ratio is said in words in the brief.
codex-cli.source: core/providers/codex-cli.js: at most 5 -i images work in Codex's image tool (codex-cli 0.166.0)

card.editPrompt: Edit the attached image: {wish} Keep everything this does not ask to change exactly as it is: the subject, the composition, the backdrop, the colours and the rendering style. Return the whole edited image.
card.editLegend: The attached image is the card to edit; change only what the brief asks.

fix.previous:
The prompt already ended with this correction, and the picture still has the problems below; write the whole correction anew, keeping what still applies:
---
{fix}
---
fix.wish: The person also asked for this, and their words outrank every finding: {wish}
fix.proposeNotes: The producer jotted these notes, which come first: keep every idea of them, in their meaning: {notes}

pick.template:
Below are {count} versions of one collectible card illustration, "{title}", all drawn from the same order. Choose the version a person would keep as the finished card.

What matters, in this order:
1. The picture is drawn correctly: no missing, extra, merged or broken arms, hands, fingers, legs or parts; no melted, garbled or impossible shapes; things are held and stand as they really would.
2. It shows what the order asks for: the right subject, its kind of staging and backdrop, and the right characters. Smaller differences from the order's wording — the exact size in the frame, the shape of an edge or a corner, an extra printed detail on a label — are not problems of this point: weigh them under point 4.
3. It holds nothing that was not ordered and that the thing does not have, such as a face on an object (a face drawn inside a printed emblem, logo or label is fine).
4. Among the versions without such problems, judge like an art director which one is better as a card: it reads at once, it is more expressive, its details are more appealing, and it is closer to the style's reference cards{refsNote}. Small measured deviations, such as colour or the hero's size against the style's rules, do not decide.
A problem of points 1–3 that you can see in a picture outweighs any number of style measurements. Under each version's number are the problems already found in it: the program's style measurements and what an earlier look saw. Check them against the pictures yourself: a measurement can be wrong, and an earlier look can miss things or see what is not there.

The order:
---
{order}
---

{versions}

The pictures follow: {refsLead}the versions, each after its version's number. Answer with JSON only: {"best": <the version number>, "reason": "<one or two short sentences: what makes this version better than the others>"}
pick.refsNote: (the first pictures are reference cards of the style with the same staging)
pick.refsLead: first the style's reference cards, each after «Reference card:», then

prompt.template: This is a {width} x {height} px card illustration. Find {hero}. Give the tightest box around all of it: include every thin part (tips, antennas, handles, rings, things sticking out of it or held by it). Exclude the backdrop, any glow or light halo behind it, its cast shadow, and the floor, table, ground or surface patch it stands on. {answer}
prompt.scene: the characters together with the props they hold or act with (the hero of this scene: «{what}»)

questions.subject: Is the main subject the kind of thing the order describes, with the parts the order names (a kettle drawn when a teapot was ordered → false; a bench drawn when a pier was ordered → false)? A part or a detail drawn a little differently (a shade of colour, a strap, how a surface is finished) is a difference to list, not a false.
questions.caption: Would a viewer who sees only the picture name its main subject with the caption's words (the caption «Lantern» under a drawn candle → false)?
questions.staging: Are the backdrop, the support and the setting the kinds the order describes, in the colours the order names for them (a brick wall ordered but a plain gradient drawn → false; a mint green wall ordered but a yellow wall drawn → false; a floor, a patch of real surface or a landscape where the order asks for one)? How high a floor or a surface reaches, the margins and the sizes are measured by the program: list them as differences, but do not answer false for them.
questions.additions: Is the image free of things that do not belong: a face on fish, animals or objects that are not the ordered characters (a mouth, a smile, brows, an expression; simple natural eyes on a fish or an animal are fine, eyes on an object are not; a face drawn inside a printed emblem, logo or label on the object, such as a smiling potato on a package, is fine); a creature or a character the order does not have; text, letters or numbers; a frame or a caption plate; a loose thing with no source or purpose (a drop, a spark, a bit or a tool floating or lying about that the order, the action or the place does not explain)? In a scene, props the action uses and things that belong to its place are fine.
questions.costume: If the order has characters: does each one wear every costume item the order names (ok = null when there are no characters)?
questions.drawing: Is the drawing free of errors a viewer would notice? Look over each character part by part: two arms and two legs attached at the right places, each hand whole, with its fingers or glove, holding things properly, no limb missing, doubled, merged or bent impossibly; both eyes look the same way, at what the action is about. Look over every repeated or matching part: cells of a panel, tiles, windows, wheels, buttons, legs of furniture, the two sides of a symmetric object — the same count, size and spacing where they should match, straight rows where the object is regular. Objects are not fused into each other and the perspective is consistent.

prompt.answer: Answer only compact JSON on one line: {json}. First write "seen": the main subject as a viewer would name it, in a few words; then "defects": every drawing error you find when you look over each character (arms, hands, legs, eyes and gaze) and over every repeated or matching part, as short phrases, an empty list when there are none; then "differences": every visible way the picture differs from the order — a thing, part, costume item, backdrop or support missing or different, something added — as short phrases, an empty list when there are none; then judge the questions from them (drawing from defects). "why" says what is wrong when ok is false and is empty otherwise. "checklist" lists only the items that do not hold, with the id as written; an empty list when all hold.

collection.what: the description of a card collection: what it is about, its mood and who it is for; every set of the collection is planned from it
collection.form: One paragraph of three to six plain sentences.

setTheme.what: the theme of one set of ten cards: what the set is about
setTheme.form: A few words on one line, like a short title.

wishes.what: the producer's wishes for a set or a whole collection of cards: what to show, what to avoid, the mood
wishes.form: One wish per line, each a short plain sentence.

cardWish.what: a wish to change one finished card illustration: what to change in the picture
cardWish.form: One or two sentences of concrete visual instructions about the picture.

cardsTheme.what: the theme of a few loose cards: what they show
cardsTheme.form: A few words on one line.

help.contextLead: What the text belongs to, for your understanding only: never repeat it in the text unless the notes say it.
help.propose:
A producer of collectible card collections needs {what}, and has not written anything for it yet. Propose that text from what it belongs to (below), as a start the producer will edit: fitting, concrete and plain, in the spirit of what is given, adding nothing that goes against it. {form} Write in {language}. Answer with the text alone: no title, no preamble, no quotes, no markdown.
{context}

context.place: The set's place in the collection: {value}
